hook.text: Organic livestock must have outdoor access, eat organic feed, and receive no routine antibiotics. The bar is higher.

buildup.text: Conventional livestock often receive antibiotics for growth promotion and live in confined indoor systems.

discovery.text: Organic rules require pasture access for ruminants and prohibit keeping poultry in permanent confinement.

twist.text: 'Outdoor access' can mean a small porch on a large barn. Organic doesn't guarantee pastoral conditions.

climax.text: Organic dairy and eggs command premium prices—but enforcement of welfare standards varies internationally.

punchline.text: Organic animal welfare is better—but 'better' isn't always 'good.'

quiz.question: What do organic livestock standards require that conventional systems often don't?
options: Outdoor access, organic feed, and no routine antibiotics
